title: Nursery Second Term
overview: Second-Term Curriculum Intent First Term established I BELONG -> I COMMUNICATE -> I NOTICE -> I REPRESENT. Second Term deliberately develops I QUESTION -> I INVESTIGATE -> I COMPARE -> I EXPLAIN -> I SOLVE. Children move beyond simply noticing their environment towards investigating relationships, making comparisons, predicting, describing what happens and attempting solutions through PLAY + LANGUAGE + INVESTIGATION + REPRESENTATION + REFLECTION. Progression From First Term First Term Second Term Progression Name familiar things Describe features and functions Answer simple questions Ask and respond to increasingly varied questions Listen to stories Retell and discuss stories Notice rhyme/sound Discriminate and manipulate sounds increasingly Make meaningful marks Use marks to communicate ideas Count meaningful objects Compare quantities and solve simple practical problems Notice shapes/patterns Describe, continue and create patterns Observe living things Compare and investigate living things Explore materials Investigate properties and changes Play with others Collaborate towards shared purposes Attempt routines Manage more routines independently Notice community Understand simple community roles and relationships Progression: NOTICE -> QUESTION -> INVESTIGATE -> TALK -> REPRESENT -> APPLY Second-Term Curriculum Map Week Big Idea Main Development 1 People Who Help Our Community Roles, service and community 2 Transport and Journeys Movement, routes and positional language 3 Materials Around Us Properties, sorting and investigation 4 Push, Pull, Roll and Slide Forces through practical exploration 5 Animals Around Us Classification, features and care 6 Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility Responsive assessment and review 7 Where Animals Live Habitats, comparison and adaptation 8 Food, Farms and Markets Origins, community and healthy experiences 9 Weather and Our Environment Observation, change and recording 10 Building, Making and Problem-Solving Design, construction and reasoning 11 Things That Work Cause, effect and simple technology 12 Stories, Music and Our Culture Narrative, language and cultural expression 13 What Have We Discovered? Reflection, explanation and consolidation Second-Term Communication & Language Spine Interaction increasingly moves from 'What is this?' towards 'Tell me about it', 'How are these different?', 'Why did you put those together?', 'What do you think might happen?', 'How could we fix it?', 'What happened first?' and 'Can you tell me another way?' The aim is sustained shared thinking, not interrogation. Phonological Awareness Progression Continue environmental sound discrimination -> instrumental sounds -> body percussion -> rhythm and rhyme -> alliteration -> voice sounds -> oral blending and segmenting experiences where developmentally appropriate. Children increasingly notice meaningful print and letters in names/environment. Sound should first be heard, enjoyed, distinguished and manipulated orally rather than turned automatically into worksheets. Second-Term Literacy Progression Children increasingly listen to longer stories, answer/ask questions, predict, retell, sequence, discuss characters, join repeated language, invent oral stories, recognise meaningful print, use drawing/marks to communicate and attempt writing-like forms naturally. Preserve THOUGHT -> LANGUAGE -> MEANING -> MARK. Second-Term Mathematics Spine Deepen number through small quantities, one-to-one correspondence, cardinality, subitising, comparison, more/fewer and composition of small numbers through practical experience. Develop pattern through copy/continue/notice/create; shape/space through construction, rotation, position, fit and routes; measure through length, height, capacity, weight and time/order. Mathematical thinking increasingly includes notice, compare, predict, check and explain. Practical Life - Second Term First Term: I CAN DO MORE. Second Term: I CAN TAKE RESPONSIBILITY. Children increasingly manage belongings, restore resources, serve, pour, wipe, sweep, wash, fold, sort, prepare, carry, fasten, care for plants, participate in food preparation, organise workspaces and appropriately help peers. Independence means adults know when to help and when to wait. Continuous Provision Maintain rich language, books, mark-making, mathematics, construction, small world, role play, creative arts, Practical Life, investigation, sensory, fine-motor and outdoor areas. Enhancements may include community role play, transport investigation, materials laboratory, ramps, habitats, market, weather station, construction workshop and simple technology. Outdoor Learning Provide large movement, routes, transport, ramps, distance comparison, construction, weather observation, plant care, animal/minibeast observation, water, measurement, collaboration, problem-solving and large-scale mark-making. Deliberately take language, mathematics and investigation outdoors. Nigerian & Owo Curriculum Connection Begin enquiry with Angel Montessori School, Owo, local roads, transport, markets, farms, foods, occupations, plants, animals, weather, materials, music, stories and Yoruba/Nigerian cultural experiences, then widen children's experience. LOCAL KNOWLEDGE IS NOT LESS ACADEMIC KNOWLEDGE. Christian Character Spine Develop Service, Patience, Responsibility, Perseverance, Gentleness, Stewardship, Gratitude, Creativity, Wisdom, Joy and Respect through real situations. Inclusion and SEND A child can investigate without necessarily explaining verbally. Responses may use gesture, choice, objects, movement, drawing, sign, home language, AAC where applicable or spoken language. Differentiate complexity, language, resources, sensory demand, physical access, time, group size and support. DIFFERENT ROUTE - SHARED ENTITLEMENT. Parent Partnership Home connections may include talking about jobs and journeys, sorting materials, rolling objects down safe slopes, discussing animals, visiting markets, preparing food, observing weather, building with boxes, reading, rhyming, meaningful counting and household routines. Parents contribute valuable knowledge about languages, culture, interests, experiences, questions and independence. Second-Term Assessment Assessment remains OBSERVE -> INTERPRET -> RESPOND. High-value observations include significant questions, spontaneous vocabulary, story retelling, rhyme noticing, quantity problem-solving, small-amount subitising, pattern continuation, construction modification, prediction, sorting explanation, successful collaboration and new independence. Assessment should answer: WHAT SHOULD WE TEACH OR PROVIDE NEXT? End-of-Second-Term Expectations Depending on starting point and development, children increasingly use richer vocabulary, sustain interaction, ask questions, describe observations, retell stories, play with sounds, communicate through marks, understand small quantities more securely, compare quantities, create patterns, use positional/comparative language, investigate materials, predict outcomes, notice cause/effect, compare living things, develop community knowledge, solve practical problems, collaborate, persist, represent ideas creatively and manage greater responsibility. These are developmental expectations, not pass/fail criteria. Progression Into Third Term First Term: BELONG -> COMMUNICATE -> NOTICE -> REPRESENT. Second Term: QUESTION -> INVESTIGATE -> COMPARE -> EXPLAIN -> SOLVE. Third Term develops CONNECT -> APPLY -> CREATE -> REFLECT -> PREPARE FOR RECEPTION, deepening growth/change, nature, wider-world knowledge, story creation, mathematical problem-solving, sound awareness, meaningful early writing, design, collaboration, independence, self-regulation and Reception transition. Nursery Second-Term Declaration We will encourage questions without always giving answers immediately. We will investigate, compare, predict, test and discuss what happened. We will read, retell, rhyme and play with sounds. We will count with understanding, notice patterns, build, test, change ideas and try again. We will explore Owo and Nigeria while widening children's world. We will develop responsibility, cooperation, creativity and thinking while protecting meaningful Early Years learning. QUESTIONERS - INVESTIGATORS - COMMUNICATORS - PROBLEM-SOLVERS - CREATORS - RESPONSIBLE LEARNERS - INDEPENDENT THINKERS HOW DOES THIS HELP THE CHILD FLOURISH? IN GOD WE TRUST. weeks.title: People Who Help Our Community
weeks.curriculumIntent: Deepen understanding of familiar occupations: what people do, why work matters and tools used.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 1 - People Who Help Our Community

items.title: Roles, service and community
items.learningIntent: Deepen understanding of familiar occupations: what people do, why work matters and tools used.
items.learningContent:
Deepen understanding of familiar occupations: what people do, why work matters and tools used. Vocabulary: community, job, work,
service, teacher, doctor, nurse, driver, farmer, trader, builder, cleaner, tool. Use community stories, environmental print, role-play
appointments/messages/lists/signs, meaningful counting, real school workers and familiar Owo occupations. Practical Life:
sweeping, wiping, serving, sorting and organising. Character: Service and Respect.
items.teachingGuidance: Deepen understanding of familiar occupations: what people do, why work matters and tools used.
items.practicalLife: sweeping, wiping, serving, sorting and organising
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Use community stories, environmental print, role-play
appointments/messages/lists/signs, meaningful counting, real school workers and familiar Owo occupations.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 1 - People Who Help Our Community

weeks.title: Transport and Journeys
weeks.curriculumIntent: Investigate movement from place to place.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 2 - Transport and Journeys

items.title: Movement, routes and positional language
items.learningIntent: Investigate movement from place to place.
items.learningContent:
Investigate movement from place to place. Vocabulary: transport, journey, road, wheel, passenger, driver, move, travel, near, far,
route, fast, slow. Describe journeys; explore forward/backward/around/through/under/over/near/far, routes, simple maps, obstacle
courses and wheeled play. Teach simple road safety and use transport genuinely encountered around Owo. Character: Patience and
Responsibility.
items.teachingGuidance: Teach simple road safety and use transport genuinely encountered around Owo.
items.nigerianAfricanContext: Teach simple road safety and use transport genuinely encountered around Owo.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 2 - Transport and Journeys

weeks.title: Materials Around Us
weeks.curriculumIntent: Investigate safe familiar materials and their properties.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 3 - Materials Around Us

items.title: Properties, sorting and investigation
items.learningIntent: Investigate safe familiar materials and their properties.
items.learningContent:
Investigate safe familiar materials and their properties. Vocabulary: wood, metal, plastic, fabric, paper, glass, hard, soft, rough,
smooth, bend, strong. Glass is adult-managed/images only. Compare, sort and explain choices; explore texture, bending, strength
and effects of water. Use information books, labels, collage, construction, textiles, folding, tearing and sorting. Character: Care and
Responsibility.
items.teachingGuidance: Use information books, labels, collage, construction, textiles, folding, tearing and sorting.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 3 - Materials Around Us

weeks.title: Push, Pull, Roll and Slide
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 4 - Push, Pull, Roll and Slide

items.title: Forces through practical exploration
items.learningContent:
Investigate movement practically. Vocabulary: push, pull, roll, slide, move, stop, fast, slow, far, near, ramp, steep. Explore cars on
ramps, balls, surfaces, pushing, pulling, rolling and sliding. Encourage prediction and description. Compare distance, speed and
ramp height informally; draw investigation records with adult-scribed comments. Character: Curiosity and Perseverance.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 4 - Push, Pull, Roll and Slide

weeks.title: Animals Around Us
weeks.curriculumIntent: Compare familiar animals using observable features.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 5 - Animals Around Us

items.title: Classification, features and care
items.learningIntent: Compare familiar animals using observable features.
items.learningContent:
Compare familiar animals using observable features. Vocabulary may include animal, mammal in adult modelling, bird, fish, insect,
feather, fur, scales, wing, leg, tail. Compare covering, movement, size, legs, sounds, food and young; sort and explain choices. Use
familiar Nigerian animals and wider examples, stories, information books, rhymes, movement, model-making and drawing.
Character: Gentleness and Care.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use
familiar Nigerian animals and wider examples, stories, information books, rhymes, movement, model-making and drawing.
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Use
familiar Nigerian animals and wider examples, stories, information books, rhymes, movement, model-making and drawing.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 5 - Animals Around Us

weeks.title: Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility
weeks.notes: Responsive review rather than formal examination.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

items.title: Responsive assessment and review
items.learningContent:
No formal examination. Revisit community, transport, materials, movement, animals, phonological awareness, storytelling, number,
shape, language, Practical Life and social development. Identify understanding, vocabulary, questions, problem-solving, number
security, cooperative play and areas needing further teaching.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.assessmentFocus:
Revisit community, transport, materials, movement, animals, phonological awareness, storytelling, number,
shape, language, Practical Life and social development.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

weeks.title: Where Animals Live
weeks.curriculumIntent: Investigate relationships between animals and environments.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 7 - Where Animals Live

items.title: Habitats, comparison and adaptation
items.learningIntent: Investigate relationships between animals and environments.
items.learningContent:
Investigate relationships between animals and environments. Vocabulary: habitat, home, nest, burrow, pond, tree, water, land,
shelter. Explore familiar associations without rigid oversimplification; sort by environment and use position language. Read habitat
texts, create story maps and construct habitats. Ask what animals might need and why. Character: Care and Stewardship.
items.teachingGuidance: Explore familiar associations without rigid oversimplification; sort by environment and use position language.
items.parentHomeConnection:
Vocabulary: habitat, home, nest, burrow, pond, tree, water, land,
shelter.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 7 - Where Animals Live

weeks.title: Food, Farms and Markets
weeks.curriculumIntent: Investigate familiar food origins and journeys.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 8 - Food, Farms and Markets

items.title: Origins, community and healthy experiences
items.learningIntent: Investigate familiar food origins and journeys.
items.learningContent:
Investigate familiar food origins and journeys. Vocabulary: farm, farmer, crop, market, trader, fruit, vegetable, grain, food, buy, sell,
money. Use locally meaningful foods such as yam, cassava, maize, rice, beans, plantain, banana, orange and vegetables as
appropriate. Explore GROW -> HARVEST -> MARKET -> HOME -> EAT experientially. Use counting, comparison, pretend money,
sorting, lists, signs and safe preparation. Character: Gratitude and Respect for Work.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use locally meaningful foods such as yam, cassava, maize, rice, beans, plantain, banana, orange and vegetables as
appropriate.
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Use locally meaningful foods such as yam, cassava, maize, rice, beans, plantain, banana, orange and vegetables as
appropriate.
items.parentHomeConnection: Explore GROW -> HARVEST -> MARKET -> HOME -> EAT experientially.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 8 - Food, Farms and Markets

weeks.title: Weather and Our Environment
weeks.curriculumIntent: Observe weather over time and notice patterns/change.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 9 - Weather and Our Environment

items.title: Observation, change and recording
items.learningIntent: Observe weather over time and notice patterns/change.
items.learningContent:
Observe weather over time and notice patterns/change. Vocabulary: weather, sunny, cloudy, rain, windy, hot, warm, cool, wet, dry,
change. Make daily observations and a simple class weather record; compare observations where meaningful. Use stories, dictated
observations, movement, sound and painting. Centre weather children actually experience rather than imported snow activities.
Character: Gratitude and Stewardship.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use stories, dictated
observations, movement, sound and painting.
items.outdoorLearning: Observe weather over time and notice patterns/change.
items.assessmentFocus: Observe weather over time and notice patterns/change.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 9 - Weather and Our Environment

weeks.title: Building, Making and Problem-Solving
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children increasingly IMAGINE -> BUILD -> TEST -> CHANGE -> TRY AGAIN.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 10 - Building, Making and Problem-Solving

items.title: Design, construction and reasoning
items.learningIntent: Children increasingly IMAGINE -> BUILD -> TEST -> CHANGE -> TRY AGAIN.
items.learningContent:
Children increasingly IMAGINE -> BUILD -> TEST -> CHANGE -> TRY AGAIN. Vocabulary: plan, build, join, strong, tall, balance,
fix, change, problem, solution. Explore shape, space, size, length, position, pattern, balance and joining materials. Draw simple
plans, test structures, explain and modify. Use open-ended making rather than identical crafts. Character: Perseverance and
Creativity.
items.teachingGuidance: Use open-ended making rather than identical crafts.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 10 - Building, Making and Problem-Solving

weeks.title: Things That Work
weeks.curriculumIntent: Investigate safe simple technology and cause-effect systems.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 11 - Things That Work

items.title: Cause, effect and simple technology
items.learningIntent: Investigate safe simple technology and cause-effect systems.
items.learningContent:
Investigate safe simple technology and cause-effect systems. Vocabulary: machine, tool, button, switch, wheel, turn, press, open,
close, work, electricity. Explore torches, mechanical toys, wheels, gears where available, buttons and adult-supported equipment.
Use first/next/then language, information texts and simple purposeful digital experiences. Never encourage independent
mains-electricity experimentation. Character: Wisdom and Responsibility.
items.teachingGuidance: Investigate safe simple technology and cause-effect systems.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 11 - Things That Work

weeks.title: Stories, Music and Our Culture
weeks.curriculumIntent: Deepen narrative language and cultural identity.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 12 - Stories, Music and Our Culture

items.title: Narrative, language and cultural expression
items.learningIntent: Deepen narrative language and cultural identity.
items.learningContent:
Deepen narrative language and cultural identity. Vocabulary: character, story, beginning, next, end, song, rhythm, beat, tradition.
Retell, sequence, predict, discuss characters, alter story parts and create oral stories. Develop rhyme, rhythm, alliteration, listening
discrimination and oral sound play. Include Yoruba/Nigerian songs, drumming, dance, drama, pattern, puppetry and Nigerian/African
stories alongside wider literature. Character: Joy, Identity and Respect.
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Include Yoruba/Nigerian songs, drumming, dance, drama, pattern, puppetry and Nigerian/African
stories alongside wider literature.
items.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 12 - Stories, Music and Our Culture

weeks.title: What Have We Discovered?
weeks.curriculumIntent: Revisit the term through investigation, explanation and representation rather than formal examination.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery Second Term / Week 13 - What Have We Discovered?

items.title: Reflection, explanation and consolidation
items.learningIntent: Revisit the term through investigation, explanation and representation rather than formal examination.
items.learningContent:
Revisit the term through investigation, explanation and representation rather than formal examination. Return to favourite
investigations, stories, sound games, number challenges, construction, community role play, animals/habitats, weather, music and
Practical Life. Review explanation, questions, vocabulary, retelling, sound awareness, meaningful marks, number, pattern,
observation, prediction, collaboration, persistence, movement, creative representation and independence.
items.teachingGuidance: Revisit the term through investigation, explanation and representation rather than formal examination.
items.outdoorLearning:
Return to favourite
investigations, stories, sound games, number challenges, construction, community role play, animals/habitats, weather, music and
Practical Life.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.assessmentFocus: Revisit the term through investigation, explanation and representation rather than formal examination.
